    Convert Biomass Units Using Taxon-Specific Conversion Factors

    ConvertBiomass.Rd

    Converts biomass measurements between different units (e.g., wet mass to dry mass, AFDM to energy) using taxon-specific conversion factors compiled from extensive literature sources. The function includes a comprehensive internal database of conversion factors for marine, and freshwater benthic taxa.

    ConvertBiomass(
  DF,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols,
  conversion,
  factors = NULL,
  na_action = "warning"
)

    Arguments

    DF

    Data frame with biomass data. Must contain:

    • A taxonomic column (matching taxon_col)

    • One or more biomass columns to convert

    taxon_col

    Character or numeric. Column name or number containing taxonomic group (e.g., "Group", "Phylum", "Class"). Must match column names in the conversion factors table (default = "Group").

    biomass_cols

    Numeric vector or character vector. Columns containing biomass values to convert. Can be column numbers (e.g., 3:5) or names (e.g., c("St1", "St2")).

    conversion

    Character. Type of conversion to apply. Options:

    • "WM_to_DM" - Wet mass to dry mass

    • "DM_to_AFDM" - Dry mass to ash-free dry mass

    • "WM_to_AFDM" - Wet mass to ash-free dry mass (direct)

    • "DM_to_Energy" - Dry mass to energy (J/mg DM)

    • "AFDM_to_Energy" - AFDM to energy (J/mg AFDM)

    • "Water_percent" - Water content as percentage

    • "Ash_percent" - Ash content as percentage

    • "AFDW_percent" - Ash-free dry weight as percentage

    • "Carbon_percent" - Organic carbon as percentage

    • "WM_to_KCal" - Wet mass to KCal (inland waters)

    factors

    Data frame with conversion factors. If NULL, uses internal database (default = NULL). If provided, must contain columns matching taxon_col and the conversion type.

    na_action

    Character. How to handle taxa without conversion factors:

    • "warning" - Issue warning and keep original values (default)

    • "remove" - Remove rows with missing factors

    • "mean" - Use mean factor across all taxa

    Value

    Data frame with converted biomass values. Original data frame structure is maintained, with biomass columns containing converted values.

    Details

    Conversion Types:

    • WM_to_DM: Wet mass → Dry mass (after drying at 60°C)

    • DM_to_AFDM: Dry mass → Ash-free dry mass (after combustion at 500°C)

    • WM_to_AFDM: Wet mass → AFDM (combined conversion)

    • DM_to_Energy: Dry mass → Energy content (Joules per mg DM)

    • AFDM_to_Energy: AFDM → Energy content (Joules per mg AFDM)

    • Water_percent: Water content as percentage of wet weight

    • Ash_percent: Ash content as percentage (of WW or DW depending on source)

    • AFDW_percent: Ash-free dry weight as percentage of wet weight

    • Carbon_percent: Organic carbon as percentage of wet weight

    • WM_to_KCal: Wet mass to KCal (for inland waters: fish = 1.0, zoobenthos/zooplankton = 0.83)

    Internal Database:

    The function includes conversion factors for major benthic taxa compiled from literature sources including:

    Marine Taxa:

    • Porifera: Sponges

    • Cnidaria: Hydrozoa, Octocorallia, Scleractinia, Actiniaria, Anthozoa

    • Nemertea: Ribbon worms

    • Annelida: Polychaeta (Errantia, Sedentaria), Oligochaeta

    • Sipuncula: Peanut worms

    • Mollusca: Gastropoda, Bivalvia, Cephalopoda, Polyplacophora

    • Arthropoda: Amphipoda, Isopoda, Decapoda, Mysidacea, Cumacea, Euphausiacea, Cirripedia

    • Echinodermata: Asteroidea, Echinoidea, Ophiuroidea, Holothuroidea, Crinoidea

    • Bryozoa: Moss animals

    • Tunicata: Ascidians

    • Pisces: Demersal, Pelagic, Mesopelagic fishes

    Freshwater/Inland Taxa:

    • Insecta Larvae: Chironomidae, Ephemeroptera, Odonata, Trichoptera

    • Fish (inland): Wet mass to dry mass (0.20), WM to KCal (1.0)

    • Zoobenthos/Zooplankton (inland): WM to DM (0.167), WM to KCal (0.83)

    Principal Literature Sources:

    • Vinogradov (1953) - Elementary chemical composition of marine organisms

    • Waters (1977) - Secondary production in inland waters

    • Brey et al. (1988) - Energy content of macrobenthic invertebrates

    • Brey (2010, 2012) - Aquatic invertebrate respiration and production

    • Ricciardi & Bourget (1998) - Weight-to-weight conversion factors

    • Eleftheriou & Basford (1989) - Macrobenthic infauna of North Sea

    • Rumohr et al. (1987) - Conversion factors for benthos

    • Lie (1968) - Production studies in Puget Sound

    • Cummins & Wuycheck (1971) - Caloric equivalents

    • Benke et al. (1999) - Length-mass relationships for freshwater invertebrates

    Shell-Free Dry Mass (SFDM):

    For molluscs, factors are based on shell-free dry mass. If your data includes shells, pre-process to remove shell weight or adjust factors accordingly.

    Note

    • Conversion factors are approximations and can vary with season, location, and individual size. For critical applications, consider using taxon-specific or site-specific factors.

    • For inland waters, use Waters (1977) factors: WM_to_DM = 0.20 (fish) or 0.167 (invertebrates).

    See also

    view_conversion_factors to explore available conversion factors.

    Functional for functional trait analysis, ExploreComm for community composition

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Convert wet mass to dry mass (marine)
biomass_data <- data.frame(
  Group = c("Amphipoda", "Bivalvia", "Polychaeta", "Asteroidea"),
  Species = c("Ampelisca", "Nucula", "Glycera", "Astropecten"),
  St1_WM = c(10.5, 25.3, 15.8, 100.2),
  St2_WM = c(12.3, 28.1, 14.2, 95.7),
  St3_WM = c(11.7, 26.8, 16.5, 102.3)
)

# Check available factors first
view_conversion_factors(conversion = "WM_to_DM")

biomass_DM <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = biomass_data,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 3:5,
  conversion = "WM_to_DM"
)

print(biomass_DM)

# Example 2: Convert dry mass to energy content
colnames(biomass_DM)[3:5] <- c("St1_DM", "St2_DM", "St3_DM")

biomass_energy <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = biomass_DM,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 3:5,
  conversion = "DM_to_Energy"
)

# Example 3: Inland waters conversion (Waters 1977)
inland_data <- data.frame(
  Group = c("Fish Inland", "Zoobenthos Inland", "Zooplankton Inland"),
  Site1 = c(50.0, 25.5, 10.2),
  Site2 = c(45.3, 30.1, 12.5)
)

inland_DM <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = inland_data,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 2:3,
  conversion = "WM_to_DM"
)

inland_KCal <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = inland_data,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 2:3,
  conversion = "WM_to_KCal"
)

# Example 4: Use custom conversion factors
my_factors <- data.frame(
  Group = c("Amphipoda", "Bivalvia"),
  WM_to_DM = c(0.22, 0.09),
  DM_to_AFDM = c(0.75, 0.85)
)

biomass_custom <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = biomass_data,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 3:5,
  conversion = "WM_to_DM",
  factors = my_factors
)

# Example 5: Search for available groups
view_conversion_factors(group_pattern = "acea")      # Crustacea
view_conversion_factors(group_pattern = "Polych")    # Polychaeta
view_conversion_factors(group_pattern = "Echino")    # Echinodermata
view_conversion_factors(conversion = "Water_percent") # Water content

# Example 6: Handle missing taxa
biomass_with_na <- data.frame(
  Group = c("Amphipoda", "UnknownGroup", "Bivalvia"),
  Species = c("Ampelisca", "Mystery", "Nucula"),
  St1 = c(10, 15, 20)
)

result <- ConvertBiomass(
  DF = biomass_with_na,
  taxon_col = "Group",
  biomass_cols = 3,
  conversion = "WM_to_DM",
  na_action = "mean"
)
} # }
